notes: THE F1 TRAP. 367.96 is printed in the largest box on the page; the payable is 69.62. derive_amount_payable and resolve_carried_balance are wired on total_printed (Task 11); prior_balance_basis comes from the pack's billing-convention table via apply_billing_conventions, registered at afterExtraction. bill_to_name (Task 8) reads the remittance stub's LEFT column off the row it shares with the payee name: EDCO prints customer and payee side by side on one set of rows, so 'EDCO WASTE & RECYCLING SERVICE' at anchor_occurrence 'mid_line' (the only one of its three occurrences that does not begin its line - the letterhead at top=33.3 and '... FOR SERVICE AT:' at top=304.0 are both line-heads) sits on the customer name's own row, and same-row + text returns the customer's cell once _apply_field drops the anchor's words. Anchoring on the VENDOR's name to read the CUSTOMER's is not GUARDRAIL 9's anchor-is-value, and it is the same anchor/occurrence remit_address already uses. No label exists anywhere near the name and every top region returns EDCO's own letterhead first, which is why this persona shipped without the selector. Moving the field off resolve_bill_to_alias's roster rung is the point: measured over all 28 real EDCO samples the selector reads SYSCO FOODS-SAN DIEGO (709223OCT25), NORTHSTAR RECYCLING CO (968397OCT25) and EDCO's own misprints NORTHSTRAY/NORTHSTART RECYCLING, so bill_to_mismatch can now fire where the roster rung could only ever agree with itself.
